## formal
Let $\Cl(p,q)$ have $p + q = 2N \ge 4$ generators $e_{1}, \dots, e_{2N}$ with $N + q$ odd, so that the pseudoscalar $I = e_{1}\cdots e_{2N}$ has $I^{2} = -1$ ($\Cl(1,3)$, $\Cl(3,1)$, $\Cl(6,0)$, $\Cl(7,1)$ are examples); $I$ commutes with the even subalgebra $E$. Put $D = 2^{N-1}$. Call two even blades $e_{S}$, $e_{T}$ (notation of \claimref{synthesis.signed-directions-and-the-integer-clifford-algebra}) equivalent when $T = S$ or $T$ is the complement of $S$; since $Ie_{S} = \pm e_{S^{c}}$ and $(Ie_{S})^{2} = -e_{S}^{2}$, each class $c$ contains, up to sign, exactly one element $h_{c}$ of square $+1$, its \emph{unit}; $h_{0} = 1$. The classes form the $\mathbb{F}_{2}$-space $V$ of even subsets modulo the full set, of dimension $2N - 2$, with $D^{2}$ elements, and $b(c,d) \in \mathbb{F}_{2}$, equal to $1$ exactly when $h_{c}$ and $h_{d}$ anticommute, is the polar form of that theorem restricted to even subsets; it is alternating and nondegenerate on $V$. The $h_{c}$ and $Ih_{c}$ form a basis of $E$; $h_{c}h_{d} = \pm h_{c+d}$ when $b(c,d) = 0$ and $\pm Ih_{c+d}$ when $b(c,d) = 1$; for $b(c,d) = 0$, $c \ne d$, write $h_{c}h_{d} = \epsilon(c,d)h_{c+d}$. A \emph{state} is an idempotent $\rho = D^{-1}\bigl(1 + \sum_{c \ne 0}x_{c}h_{c}\bigr)$ of $E$ with rational or real coordinates $x_{c} = D\langle\rho h_{c}\rangle_{0}$. Let $\Gamma$ be the group of automorphisms of $E$ generated by the conjugations by the \emph{quarter-turn elements} $R_{c} = 1 + k_{c}$, $k_{c} = Ih_{c}$ a blade with $k_{c}^{2} = -1$, $c \ne 0$ (unnormalised; $R_{c}^{-1} = \tfrac12(1 - k_{c})$), and for a function $f$ of states let $\langle f\rangle_{\Gamma}(\rho)$ be the mean of $f(g\rho g^{-1})$ over $g \in \Gamma$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The group; proved, the two orders computed.)} Conjugation by $R_{c}$ fixes $I$ and $h_{d}$ when $b(c,d) = 0$ and sends $h_{d}$ to $-Ih_{d}h_{c} = \pm h_{c+d}$ when $b(c,d) = 1$: on $V$ it is the transvection $d \mapsto d + b(c,d)c$. $\Gamma$ is finite, contains the conjugation by every $h_{c}$ (which is $R_{c}^{2}$ up to the central factor $2I$), carries states to states, and acts transitively on the nonzero classes and on the ordered pairs $(c,d)$ of distinct nonzero classes with $b(c,d) = 0$. For $N = 2$ it has order $24$ (in $\Cl(1,3)$ the $R_{c}$ are $1$ plus the spatial bivectors and $\Gamma$ is the rotation group of the cube acting on the relative vectors) and for $\Cl(6,0)$ order $11520$ (both computed; they equal $2^{2N-2}$, the sign flips, times the order of the symplectic group of $V$, given the classical theorem, not used here, that transvections generate it). $R_{c}$ is a rotor exactly when $k_{c}$ is a bivector: every generator for $2N \le 6$ ($\Cl(1,3)$, $\Cl(3,1)$, $\Cl(6,0)$). For $2N \ge 8$ the generators include blades of grade $4$ or $6$, which are not versors, and for grade $4$ ($\Cl(7,1)$: $35$ of $63$) $R_{c}\tilde R_{c} = 2k_{c}$ is not a scalar; the bivector rotors alone are not transitive on the classes ($\Cl(7,1)$: orbits $7$, $21$, $35$; $\Cl(10,0)$: $45$, $210$; computed) and are not a design. The statement is for signatures with $I^{2} = -1$, where the unit of the averages is the pseudoscalar.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Two identities of a state; proved.)} $\sum_{c \ne 0}x_{c}^{2} = D - 1$, and for every $u \ne 0$, $\sum\epsilon(c,d)x_{c}x_{d} = (D - 2)x_{u}$, the sum over the $\tfrac12D^{2} - 2$ ordered pairs of nonzero classes with $c + d = u$ and $b(c,d) = 0$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Moments to order three; proved.)} For every state and all nonzero classes $c, d, e$:
\[
\langle x_{c}\rangle_{\Gamma} = 0, \qquad \langle x_{c}x_{d}\rangle_{\Gamma} = \frac{\delta_{cd}}{D + 1}, \qquad \langle x_{c}x_{d}x_{e}\rangle_{\Gamma} = \begin{cases}\dfrac{2\,\epsilon(c,d)}{(D + 1)(D + 2)} & e = c + d,\ c \ne d,\ b(c,d) = 0,\\[1ex] 0 & \text{otherwise.}\end{cases}
\]
The values do not depend on the state averaged. \emph{Corollary (a set of modes on a parity sector).} For a proper subset $A$ of $2a$ of the generators the even blades of $A$ are $\tfrac12 d_{A}^{2}$ distinct classes, $d_{A} = 2^{a}$, and the purity of a state on the even part of $A$ is $d_{A}^{-1}\sum x_{c}^{2}$ over them; by the second moment its mean is $d_{A}^{-1}\bigl(1 + (\tfrac12 d_{A}^{2} - 1)/(D + 1)\bigr) = (d_{A} + d_{B})/(d_{A}d_{B} + 2)$ with $d_{A}d_{B} = 2D$: $\tfrac23$ at four generators. It follows from (iii) and not from (v).
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Every invariant measure to order three; proved; the imported Fact is a cross-check.)} Since the $\Gamma$-mean of every monomial of degree at most three is the same number for every state, every probability measure on states that is invariant under $\Gamma$ has the moments of (iii): its moment is the integral of the $\Gamma$-mean. The unitarily invariant measure is one such measure, so for $D$ a power of two its moments to order three are derived here. Identify $E$ with the $D \times D$ matrices over $\mathrm{span}\{1, I\}$, the $h_{c}$ Hermitian of square one and trace $D\langle h_{c}\rangle_{0}$, a state with $\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}$, $x_{c} = \bra{\psi}h_{c}\ket{\psi}$. The values of (iii) are those that Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-haar-moments-of-random-pure-state} gives for $n \le 3$, $\sum_{\sigma}\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(P_{\sigma}\,h_{c}\otimes h_{d}\otimes h_{e}\bigr)/(D(D+1)(D+2))$ and its analogue with two factors. Since the monomials of degree at most three in the $x_{c}$ span the polynomials of degree at most three in $\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}$, the $\Gamma$-orbit of every state is a design of order three: the mean of $(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})^{\otimes n}$ over the orbit is the invariant mean for $n = 1, 2, 3$. Each $\Gamma$-orbit is itself such a measure. No statement is made at order four.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Mean purity of a matrix factor; proved.)} Let $W \subset V$ be a subspace of dimension $2r$ on which $b$ is nondegenerate, $m = 2^{r}$ and $n = D/m$; the $h_{c}$, $c \in W$, span over $\mathrm{span}\{1, I\}$ a subalgebra isomorphic to the $m \times m$ matrices, and the purity of a state on it is $P_{W} = m^{-1}\sum_{c \in W}x_{c}^{2}$ (with $x_{0} = 1$). Then for every state
\[
\langle P_{W}\rangle_{\Gamma} = \frac1m\Bigl(1 + \frac{m^{2} - 1}{D + 1}\Bigr) = \frac{m + n}{mn + 1},
\]
the mean purity of the unitarily invariant measure on $\C^{m}\otimes\C^{n}$ by (iv), the value of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-haar-average-purity}, here a finite sum, for dimensions $m$, $n$ that are powers of two and for no others: a comparison stated for all $m$, $n$ can rest on this clause only where its dimensions are powers of two. The even blades of a proper subset of the generators do not form such a $W$ (they are $\tfrac12 m^{2}$ classes, not $m^{2}$), and their purity is not covered by this clause.
\end{enumerate}

## technical
The even subalgebra of a Clifford algebra with an even number $2N$ of generators and a pseudoscalar of square $-1$ is a complex matrix algebra whose imaginary unit is the pseudoscalar. Its even blades, taken up to that unit, are the Pauli operators of $N - 1$ qubits, and each has a version $k$ of square $-1$, so $1 + k$ is a real invertible element, a quarter turn about the blade $k$; it is a rotor exactly when $k$ is a bivector, which is every case up to six generators and not beyond. The conjugations by these elements form a finite group (the Clifford group of quantum information, modulo phases). The result is that averaging any pure state over this group gives the first three moments of every measure invariant under the group, the unitarily invariant one among them, with a proof that uses three facts only: conjugation by a blade flips signs, the quarter-turn elements act on the classes of blades as the transvections of a nondegenerate alternating form and so mix them transitively, and a pure state is an idempotent. The second moment gives Lubkin's mean purity $(m + n)/(mn + 1)$ for a matrix factor as a finite sum, for dimensions that are powers of two. Orders four and above, and the parity-superselected purity of a set of modes, are outside the statement.

## lay
Several entropy comparisons in the store borrow, from the literature, the average behaviour of a quantum state chosen completely at random. A completely random choice means an average over a continuous infinity of states. This result shows that for the quantities of second and third order, which include the average purity those comparisons use, the same numbers come out of an average over a finite list of states: the ones reached from any starting state by quarter turns about the blades of the algebra (rotations in planes when there are at most six generators). For two qubits the list has at most 11520 entries. The finite average is carried out inside the algebra the series already uses, with its own unit in place of the imaginary number. It reproduces the borrowed numbers exactly up to third order and makes no claim beyond that.

## one-liner
In an even subalgebra with $2N$ generators and $I^{2} = -1$, the finite group generated by the quarter-turn elements $1 + Ih_{c}$ (rotors for $2N \le 6$ only) averages every state to $\langle x_{c}x_{d}\rangle = \delta_{cd}/(D+1)$ and $\langle x_{c}x_{d}x_{c+d}\rangle = 2\epsilon/((D+1)(D+2))$, $D = 2^{N-1}$, the moments to order three of every measure invariant under the group, the unitarily invariant one among them, so the mean purity of a matrix factor is Lubkin's $(m+n)/(mn+1)$ by a finite sum; order four is not claimed.

proofs.proof-main.tex:
\emph{Setting.} For $2N$ generators $I^{2} = (-1)^{N(2N-1)}(-1)^{q} = (-1)^{N+q}$, so $I^{2} = -1$ exactly when $N + q$ is odd; $I$ anticommutes with every $e_{i}$ and commutes with $E$. By clause (ii) of \claimref{synthesis.signed-directions-and-the-integer-clifford-algebra}, $e_{S}e_{T} = \pm e_{S\triangle T}$, $e_{S}^{2} = \pm 1$ and $e_{S}e_{T} = (-1)^{b(S,T)}e_{T}e_{S}$ with $b(S,T) = |S||T| + |S\cap T| \bmod 2$. $Ie_{S} = \pm e_{S^{c}}$ and $(Ie_{S})^{2} = I^{2}e_{S}^{2} = -e_{S}^{2}$, so of $e_{S}$ and $Ie_{S}$ exactly one has square $+1$. For even $S$, $T$ the form $b(S,T) = |S\cap T| \bmod 2$ is alternating, the full set is in its radical, and by clause (iii) of that theorem the radical of $b$ on all subsets is trivial for an even number of generators, so the radical on even subsets (the orthogonal complement of the full set) is the full set alone: $b$ is nondegenerate on $V$. The $2D^{2} = 2^{2N-1}$ elements $h_{c}$, $Ih_{c}$ are the even blades up to sign, a basis of $E$. If $b(c,d) = 0$, $(h_{c}h_{d})^{2} = 1$, so $h_{c}h_{d} = \pm h_{c+d}$; if $b(c,d) = 1$, $(h_{c}h_{d})^{2} = -1$, so $h_{c}h_{d} = \pm Ih_{c+d}$. Hence $\langle h_{c}h_{d}\rangle_{0} = \delta_{cd}$, and $x_{c} = D\langle\rho h_{c}\rangle_{0}$.

\emph{(i).} Put $k = Ih_{c}$, $k^{2} = -1$. If $h_{d}$ commutes with $h_{c}$ it commutes with $R_{c}$. If it anticommutes, $R_{c}h_{d}R_{c}^{-1} = \tfrac12(1 + k)h_{d}(1 - k) = \tfrac12 h_{d}(1 - k)^{2} = -h_{d}k = -Ih_{d}h_{c}$, which is $\pm h_{c+d}$ by the setting. So conjugation by $R_{c}$ permutes the set $\{\pm h_{d}\}$ and fixes $I$; an automorphism in $\Gamma$ is determined by its action on that finite set, so $\Gamma$ is finite. $R_{c}^{2} = 2k$ and $I$ is central in $E$, so conjugation by $h_{c}$ lies in $\Gamma$; it multiplies $h_{d}$ by $(-1)^{b(c,d)}$. An automorphism carries idempotents to idempotents and $\Gamma$ preserves the real span of the $h_{c}$ and the scalar part, so states go to states. Transitivity. Write $t_{c}$ for the transvection of $c$. If $c \ne c'$ are nonzero and $b(c,c') = 1$, $t_{c+c'}(c) = c'$. If $b(c,c') = 0$, the functionals $b(\cdot,c)$, $b(\cdot,c')$ are independent, so there is $w$ with $b(w,c) = b(w,c') = 1$, and $t_{w+c'}t_{c+w}(c) = c'$. For pairs: given $(c,d)$ and $(c',d')$ with $b = 0$, first move $c$ to $c'$; then $d$, $d'$ lie in $c'^{\perp}\setminus\{0, c'\}$ and it suffices to move $d$ to $d'$ by transvections $t_{v}$ with $b(v,c') = 0$, which fix $c'$. If $b(d,d') = 1$, $v = d + d'$ does it. If $b(d,d') = 0$ and $d \ne d'$, choose $w$ with $b(w,c') = 0$, $b(w,d) = b(w,d') = 1$: the three functionals are independent unless $d' = d + c'$, in which case the third condition follows from the first two and $c'$, $d$ are independent; then $t_{w+d'}t_{d+w}$ carries $d$ to $d'$ and both factors fix $c'$. The orders $24$ and $11520$ are computed by closing the signed permutations (check). A generator with $k_{c}$ a bivector is a rotor; for $k_{c}$ of grade four the reverse fixes $k_{c}$ and $R_{c}\tilde R_{c} = (1 + k_{c})^{2} = 2k_{c}$; the orbits of the bivector generators alone in $\Cl(7,1)$ and $\Cl(10,0)$ are computed in the check.

\emph{(ii).} The scalar part of $\rho^{2} = \rho$ is $D^{-2}(1 + \sum_{c\ne0}x_{c}^{2}) = D^{-1}$. The coefficient of $h_{u}$, $u \ne 0$, in $\rho^{2}$ is $D^{-2}\bigl(2x_{u} + \sum_{c+d=u}x_{c}x_{d}\,[h_{c}h_{d}]_{h_{u}}\bigr)$ over nonzero $c$, $d$; pairs with $b(c,d) = 1$ contribute to $Ih_{u}$ only, and there $(c,d)$ and $(d,c)$ cancel, as they must since $\rho$ has no $Ih_{u}$ part. Equating with $x_{u}/D$ gives the second identity. The pairs: $c \in u^{\perp}\setminus\{0, u\}$, and $|u^{\perp}| = \tfrac12D^{2}$.

\emph{(iii).} Write $\langle\cdot\rangle$ for $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\Gamma}$; it is invariant under replacing $\rho$ by $g\rho g^{-1}$, $g \in \Gamma$. The coordinates of $g\rho g^{-1}$ are $x_{c}(g\rho g^{-1}) = D\langle\rho\,g^{-1}(h_{c})\rangle_{0}$. \emph{Sign flips.} For a monomial $x_{c_{1}}\cdots x_{c_{j}}$ with $c_{1} + \dots + c_{j} \ne 0$ there is $u$ with $b(u, c_{1} + \dots + c_{j}) = 1$, and conjugation by $h_{u}$ multiplies the monomial by $-1$: its mean is $0$. This gives $\langle x_{c}\rangle = 0$, $\langle x_{c}x_{d}\rangle = 0$ for $c \ne d$, and $\langle x_{c}x_{d}x_{e}\rangle = 0$ unless $e = c + d$ (in particular it vanishes when two of the three classes coincide, the third being nonzero). \emph{Second moment.} By transitivity on nonzero classes $\langle x_{c}^{2}\rangle = a$ does not depend on $c$ (a $g^{-1}$ carrying $h_{c}$ to $\pm h_{c'}$ gives $x_{c}^{2}(g\rho g^{-1}) = x_{c'}^{2}(\rho)$), and the first identity of (ii) gives $(D^{2} - 1)a = D - 1$, $a = 1/(D+1)$. \emph{Third moment, anticommuting.} Let $e = c + d$, $b(c,d) = 1$; then $b(c,e) = b(d,e) = 1$. Conjugation by $R_{e}$ sends $h_{c} \mapsto -Ih_{c}h_{e} = sh_{d}$, $h_{d} \mapsto -Ih_{d}h_{e} = s'h_{c}$ and fixes $h_{e}$; multiplying, $ss'h_{d}h_{c} = I^{2}h_{c}h_{e}h_{d}h_{e} = h_{c}h_{d} = -h_{d}h_{c}$, so $ss' = -1$ and $x_{c}x_{d}x_{e}$ changes sign: its mean is $0$. \emph{Third moment, commuting.} Let $b(c,d) = 0$, $c \ne d$, $e = c + d$ and $T(c,d) = \epsilon(c,d)x_{c}x_{d}x_{c+d}$. If $g^{-1}(h_{c}) = \sigma h_{c'}$ and $g^{-1}(h_{d}) = \tau h_{d'}$ then $g^{-1}(h_{c+d}) = \epsilon(c,d)\sigma\tau\,h_{c'}h_{d'} = \epsilon(c,d)\epsilon(c',d')\sigma\tau\,h_{c'+d'}$, so $T(c,d)(g\rho g^{-1}) = T(c',d')(\rho)$. By transitivity on commuting pairs $\langle T(c,d)\rangle = \kappa$ for all of them. Multiply the second identity of (ii) by $x_{u}$ and average: $(\tfrac12D^{2} - 2)\kappa = (D - 2)a$, so for $D > 2$, $\kappa = 2/((D+1)(D+2))$; for $D = 2$ there is no commuting pair. All values are independent of $\rho$.

\emph{Corollary to (iii).} For a proper subset $A$ of $2a$ generators no even subset of $A$ has its complement in $A$, so the $2^{2a-1} = \tfrac12d_{A}^{2}$ even subsets are distinct classes, the empty one being $0$; the restriction of a state to the algebra they span has purity $d_{A}^{-1}\sum x_{c}^{2}$ in the trace of the $d_{A}$-dimensional module of $A$, and (iii) gives the mean $d_{A}^{-1}(1 + (\tfrac12d_{A}^{2} - 1)/(D+1)) = (D + \tfrac12d_{A}^{2})/(d_{A}(D+1)) = (d_{B} + d_{A})/(d_{A}d_{B} + 2)$ with $D = \tfrac12d_{A}d_{B}$.

\emph{(iv).} With $I^{2} = -1$ and $I$ central, $E$ is a central simple algebra over $\mathrm{span}\{1, I\}$ of dimension $D^{2}$, the $D\times D$ matrices; the adjoint is the real-linear map fixing every $h_{c}$ and negating every $Ih_{c}$; it is an anti-automorphism because $h_{c}h_{d} = \pm h_{c+d}$ for commuting and $\pm Ih_{c+d}$ for anticommuting units, and $\langle xx^{\dagger}\rangle_{0}$ is the sum of the squared coefficients of $x$; the trace is $D$ times the part along $1$ and $I$. \emph{Invariant measures.} Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on states invariant under $\Gamma$ and $f$ a monomial of degree at most three. Then $\int f\,d\mu = \int\langle f\rangle_{\Gamma}\,d\mu$ by invariance, and $\langle f\rangle_{\Gamma}$ is by (iii) a constant, so $\int f\,d\mu$ is that constant. The unitarily invariant measure is invariant under conjugation by every invertible element that preserves the adjoint up to scale, the $R_{c}$ among them ($R_{c}R_{c}^{\dagger} = (1 + k_{c})(1 - k_{c}) = 2$). What follows compares with the imported formula as a cross-check. The formula of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-haar-moments-of-random-pure-state} is the sum over permutations of the products of cycle traces, divided by $D(D+1)\cdots(D+n-1)$. For two factors $\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}h_{c}\operatorname{Tr}h_{d} + \operatorname{Tr}h_{c}h_{d}\bigr)/(D(D+1)) = \delta_{cd}/(D+1)$. For three factors every term of the sum over $S_{3}$ containing the trace of a single unit vanishes, the transpositions give $\operatorname{Tr}(h_{c}h_{d})\operatorname{Tr}h_{e} = 0$, and the two three-cycles give $\operatorname{Tr}(h_{c}h_{d}h_{e}) + \operatorname{Tr}(h_{c}h_{e}h_{d})$, which is $2\epsilon(c,d)D$ for a commuting pair with $e = c + d$, zero for an anticommuting pair with $e = c + d$ (the two orders differ by a sign) and zero otherwise; divided by $D(D+1)(D+2)$ these are the values of (iii). A polynomial of degree $n$ in the entries of $\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}$ is a combination of products of $n$ numbers $\operatorname{Tr}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}h_{c})$, $c \in V$, because the $h_{c}$ span the matrices; so equality on monomials of degree at most three, including those with $x_{0} = 1$, is the design property of order three. The check recomputes both sides independently.

\emph{(v).} A subspace $W$ on which $b$ is nondegenerate has a symplectic basis; the corresponding units generate $r$ mutually commuting copies of the algebra of two anticommuting units of square one, the $2\times2$ matrices over $\mathrm{span}\{1, I\}$, so the $h_{c}$, $c \in W$, span the $m\times m$ matrices, a factor with commutant the $n\times n$ matrices. The reduced state of $\rho$ on it is $m^{-1}\sum_{c\in W}x_{c}h_{c}$ (it has the same expectation on every $h_{c}$, $c \in W$), with purity $m^{-1}\sum_{c\in W}x_{c}^{2}$. By (iii), $\langle P_{W}\rangle = m^{-1}(1 + (m^{2} - 1)/(D + 1)) = (D + m^{2})/(m(D + 1)) = (m + n)/(mn + 1)$ with $D = mn$. This is the value of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-haar-average-purity} at $(m, n)$. The even blades of a proper subset $A$ of the generators, $|A| = 2a$, are $2^{2a-1}$ distinct classes, half of $m^{2}$ for $m = 2^{a}$, and do not span a matrix factor.
